nodes.title: Critical Thinking as Governed Inquiry
nodes.summary: Critical thinking governs movement from situation through map, argument, judgment, authorization, repair, and REOPEN.
nodes.canonicalClaim: Good argumentation is necessary but not sufficient for responsible inquiry.

nodes.title: Map, Argument, Judgment
nodes.summary: A map represents a situation; an argument connects reasons to a claim; a judgment adopts a bounded conclusion for a purpose.
nodes.canonicalClaim: Map ≠ Argument ≠ Judgment.

nodes.title: Traditional Critical Thinking and the FSP Extension
nodes.summary: FSP retains logic, argument analysis, evidence, inference forms, fallacy analysis, counterexamples, and source evaluation, then makes representation, standing, authorization, repair, and reopening explicit.
nodes.canonicalClaim: FSP extends rather than replaces traditional critical thinking.

nodes.title: Twelve-Tool Functional Grammar
nodes.summary: The twelve Ethics Tools form a critical-thinking ecology in which each protects a different transition or vulnerability.
nodes.canonicalClaim: Problem topology → Tool selection → Tool sequencing → bounded judgment.

nodes.title: Failure-Mode Atlas
nodes.summary: Begin with a recognizable reasoning symptom, identify the likely failure mode, then route to the Tool and claim ceiling that can improve the map.
nodes.canonicalClaim: Failure diagnosis routes inquiry; it does not decide the verdict.

nodes.title: Judgment, Standing, and Authorization
nodes.summary: A supported conclusion can leave open whether an actor has standing to recommend, impose, classify, constrain, or intervene.
nodes.canonicalClaim: Supported judgment ≠ unrestricted authorization.

nodes.title: Repair and REOPEN
nodes.summary: A repair targets an identified failure mode and preserves explicit conditions for reopening.
nodes.canonicalClaim: Current warrant must preserve a route for correction.

nodes.title: Cross-Domain Applications
nodes.summary: The same inquiry grammar can travel across ethics, science, history, institutional reasoning, and ordinary argument while domain ontology remains distinct.
nodes.canonicalClaim: Shared grammar ≠ shared ontology.

nodes.title: Formal Tool and Transition Architecture
nodes.summary: A Tool has a canonical question, admissible input, failure mode, output, claim ceiling, and neighboring transitions.
nodes.canonicalClaim: A revised inquiry state cannot claim more standing than its licensed transition earns.

nodes.title: Source Ledger and Comparator Notes
nodes.summary: Historical sources, scholarly reconstruction, contemporary project sources, and FSP reconstruction remain distinguishable.
nodes.canonicalClaim: Historical source ≠ scholarly reconstruction ≠ FSP reconstruction.

nodes.title: Map ≠ World ≠ Person
nodes.summary: Inquiry operates through representations; a useful map is not identical to the world or person represented.
nodes.canonicalClaim: Map ≠ World ≠ Person.

nodes.title: Possibility ≠ Recommendation ≠ Authorization
nodes.summary: Generating an option does not recommend it; recommending it does not authorize implementation.
nodes.canonicalClaim: Generate ≠ Recommend ≠ Authorize.

nodes.title: Claim Ceiling
nodes.summary: A claim ceiling marks the strongest conclusion the current evidence, Tool, model, or reconstruction licenses.
nodes.canonicalClaim: Ask: what does not yet follow?

nodes.title: Tool ≠ Verdict
nodes.summary: A Tool changes visibility, constrains inference, or exposes a distinction without automatically deciding the case.
nodes.canonicalClaim: Tool → better inquiry, not automatic answer.

nodes.title: REOPEN
nodes.summary: REOPEN specifies evidence, challenge, changed conditions, failed predictions, or unintended consequences that return a settlement to inquiry.
nodes.canonicalClaim: Current judgment ≠ final closure.

nodes.title: Authorial Return
nodes.summary: Inquiry aids may reconstruct, compare, simulate, and expose; final judgment returns to the human inquirer as authored judgment.
nodes.canonicalClaim: Cognitive support ≠ outsourced authorship.

nodes.title: Progressive Disclosure
nodes.summary: Presentation may simplify while semantic identity remains stable across reader depths.
nodes.canonicalClaim: Presentation compression ≠ semantic mutation.

nodes.title: Shared Grammar ≠ Shared Ontology
nodes.summary: The same inquiry transition may recur across domains without implying that the domains contain the same kinds of entities.
nodes.canonicalClaim: Shared grammar ≠ shared domain ontology.

nodes.title: One Canonical Owner, Many Projections
nodes.summary: Reusable concepts have one canonical owner while books, courses, apps, and labs provide pedagogical projections.
nodes.canonicalClaim: Projection ≠ competing canonical definition.

nodes.title: Return to Lived Doing
nodes.summary: Formalization exists to improve situated human inquiry and action rather than replace them.
nodes.canonicalClaim: The endpoint is better Doing, not formalism for its own sake.

nodes.title: Scientific Atlas
nodes.summary: Compare five canonical inquiry dossiers through shared state, transition, probe, source-ledger, and claim-ceiling fields.
nodes.canonicalClaim: Shared comparative fields support disciplined comparison without implying historical or ontological identity.

nodes.title: Twelve Tools
nodes.summary: Browse the twelve canonical critical-thinking Tools as functional inquiry operators, each with a canonical question, failure modes, historical projection, and claim ceiling.
nodes.canonicalClaim: The Tool Rack is a functional ecology, not a single-method checklist and not twelve competing verdicts.

nodes.title: Critical Thinking
nodes.summary: Enter the critical-thinking architecture through named concepts, Tool functions, failure modes, cases, and claim ceilings rather than internal IDs.
nodes.canonicalClaim: Critical thinking is governed inquiry from representation through judgment, authorization, repair, and REOPEN.

nodes.title: FSP Constitution
nodes.summary: Browse the frozen constitutional distinctions that govern FSP inquiry across domains.
nodes.canonicalClaim: Constitutional rules constrain what the system may represent, infer, authorize, and claim.

nodes.title: Failure Atlas
nodes.summary: Browse sixteen common inquiry failures by recognizable symptom, diagnostic question, primary Tool, and claim ceiling.
nodes.canonicalClaim: Failure diagnosis improves inquiry by identifying what kind of reasoning work is needed; it does not itself determine a verdict.

nodes.title: FSP Encyclopedia Home
nodes.summary: Universal, domain-neutral entrance to Full-Stack Philosophy, its domains, cross-domain resources, and reader depths.
nodes.canonicalClaim: The Encyclopedia begins from plural domains and a corrigible shared governance grammar; Critical Thinking is one first-class entrance rather than the universal front door.

nodes.title: Why FSP?
nodes.summary: A quick public explanation of why FSP extends critical thinking into governed inquiry across representations, domains, institutions, and correction.
nodes.canonicalClaim: FSP helps heterogeneous inquiries become mutually inspectable without requiring one shared ontology, method, or worldview.

nodes.title: Extended Critical Thinking and Joint Task Spaces
nodes.summary: Standard-depth explanation of ABCD, Tools, Firewalls, claim ceilings, REOPEN, cooperation without convergence, and Joint Task Spaces.
nodes.canonicalClaim: Extended Critical Thinking embeds traditional critical thinking inside a governed inquiry architecture that can support cooperation without convergence.

nodes.title: Translation Governance and Cross-Domain Interoperability
nodes.summary: Deep/Formal reference for provenance, remainder, standing, authorization, translation invariants, and grammar-level REOPEN.
nodes.canonicalClaim: Cross-domain interoperability requires governed translation that preserves provenance, remainder, standing, claim ceilings, authorization state, and correction routes.

nodes.title: Domains
nodes.summary: Enter the Encyclopedia through domain libraries with their own native topologies, resources, evidence, and maturity states.
nodes.canonicalClaim: Universal navigation is domain-neutral; domain-native navigation may differ by field.

nodes.title: Resources
nodes.summary: Cross-domain canonical and public resources for orientation, critical thinking, Tools, failures, cases, and formal governance.
nodes.canonicalClaim: Shared resources support cross-domain inspection without replacing domain-native inquiry.

nodes.title: Routes
nodes.summary: Books, courses, laboratories, and workspaces that select and sequence canonical resources for particular purposes.
nodes.canonicalClaim: Route ≠ canonical owner.

nodes.title: About
nodes.summary: How the FSP Encyclopedia is organized, governed, progressively disclosed, and kept corrigible.
nodes.canonicalClaim: The Encyclopedia is a governed and revisable architecture, not a final ontology of inquiry.

nodes.title: Florida Nursing-Home Joint Task Space
nodes.summary: A cross-domain Gulf Pines pilot testing cooperation without convergence across residents, families, staffing, clinical/public health, regulation, institutions, historical evidence, and ethical judgment.
nodes.canonicalClaim: A governed Joint Task Space can coordinate heterogeneous evidence, standing, constraints, and action without collapsing them into one ontology or one authority.

nodes.title: Early Signal
nodes.summary: Early symptom cluster with uncertain cause, scale, and staffing implications.
nodes.canonicalClaim: Early cluster ≠ confirmed facility-wide outbreak.

nodes.title: Widening Map
nodes.summary: Confirmed transmission widens the map to resident capability, family knowledge, and staffing feasibility.
nodes.canonicalClaim: Confirmed transmission ≠ one uniform restriction.

nodes.title: Intervention Pressure
nodes.summary: Rising cases turn the task toward legitimacy, authorization, unequal burden, and review conditions.
nodes.canonicalClaim: Benefit ≠ authorization; uniform rule ≠ equal practical burden.

nodes.title: Revised Bounded Judgment
nodes.summary: Declining transmission and visible intervention harms require differentiated recovery and narrowed authorization.
nodes.canonicalClaim: Improved conditions ≠ final closure.

nodes.title: Standing and Authorization
nodes.summary: Layer 2 governance ledger distinguishing evidential authority, moral standing, legal/institutional authority, recommendation standing, authorization standing, implementation power, and review.
nodes.canonicalClaim: A Joint Task Space must govern the relations among evidence, standing, recommendation, authorization, implementation, and review rather than collapse participants into generic stakeholders.

nodes.title: Translation and Remainder
nodes.summary: Layer 3 governance for cross-domain translation, provenance, observation/inference status, remainder, translation loss, and remainder debt.
nodes.canonicalClaim: Cross-domain interoperability requires preserving domain-native meaning, provenance, claim ceilings, and remainder rather than treating translation as lossless identity.

nodes.title: Repair, Strategy Families, and Sequencing
nodes.summary: Layer 4 governance for strategy families, sequencing, reversibility, repair bundles, Generate/Recommend/Authorize separation, stop conditions, and repair debt.
nodes.canonicalClaim: FSP moves from diagnosed pressure to governed strategy families, sequenced repair, bounded authorization, monitored implementation, and REOPEN rather than directly from problem to solution.

nodes.title: Institutional Amplification and Regulatory REOPEN
nodes.summary: Layer 5 governance for facility-level amplification, policy sedimentation, metric governance, upward evidence translation, regulatory remainder debt, and multi-level REOPEN.
nodes.canonicalClaim: Institutional amplification turns judgments into environments, so governance must track what changes when bounded local judgments become policy, metrics, defaults, or regulation and how those structures remain corrigible.

nodes.title: Five-Layer Vertical Integration
nodes.summary: Worked vertical walkthrough showing how one Gulf Pines issue moves through state, standing, translation, repair, institutional amplification, and REOPEN without conceptual duplication.
nodes.canonicalClaim: A usable Joint Task Space is one corrigible inquiry in which state, standing, translation, repair, and amplification remain distinct but continuously communicate.

nodes.title: Five-Layer Integration Freeze Gate
nodes.summary: Freeze-and-test gate for Gulf Pines five-layer usability, non-duplication, Quick/Standard/Deep compression, Return/REOPEN integrity, and cross-layer carry-forward.
nodes.canonicalClaim: The Gulf Pines five-layer architecture is provisionally frozen as a canonical Joint Task Space reference implementation, subject to explicit reopen conditions under cross-domain stress or usability failure.

nodes.title: Asteria-2047 Cross-Domain Comparator
nodes.summary: Planetary-defense stress test of the Gulf Pines five-layer grammar under long-horizon uncertainty, model dependence, distributed authority, future-person standing, irreversibility, and risk transfer.
nodes.canonicalClaim: The five-layer Joint Task Space grammar appears portable across Gulf Pines and Asteria-2047, with pressure concentrated inside existing layers rather than requiring a sixth layer.

nodes.title: Whole-Encyclopedia Coherence Audit
nodes.summary: Public-coherence gate testing Home, Why FSP, domain entry, worked cases, Quick/Standard/Deep depth integrity, canonical ownership, Core/Formal boundaries, Return, and development-history firewall.
nodes.canonicalClaim: The current FSP Encyclopedia public shell is coherent enough to serve as a baseline, subject to targeted repairs and future usability testing.

nodes.title: Transformation Observatory — Guided Pilot
nodes.summary: Interactive worked-case reader for learning how FSP inspects transformations. It does not automatically analyze arbitrary questions; use the Workbench to author your own map.
nodes.canonicalClaim: FSP makes transformations inspectable by exposing states, transition warrants, access relations, possibility changes, multi-scale consequences, claim ceilings, and REOPEN conditions without requiring shared domain ontology.

nodes.title: Transformation Observatory Guide
nodes.summary: Plain-language guide to what the current Guided Pilot is, what it is not, and how to benefit from its worked cases before building a user-authored map.
nodes.canonicalClaim: The Guided Pilot teaches transformation inspection through worked cases; it does not automatically analyze arbitrary user questions.

nodes.title: Transformation Observatory Workbench
nodes.summary: Bring-your-own-question authoring surface for constructing states, transition claims, evidence, assumptions, alternatives, claim ceilings, possibility changes, and REOPEN conditions.
nodes.canonicalClaim: The Workbench makes a user-authored transformation map inspectable; it does not yet infer or validate that map automatically.

tools.title: Ethical Attention / First Map Audit
tools.function: Inspect the representation before reasoning confidently from it.
tools.question: What happened? What am I adding? What am I failing to notice?

tools.title: Examination / Reason-Giving Audit
tools.function: Test claims, reasons, explanatory direction, and inferential licenses.
tools.question: What is the claim? What reasons support it? What follows, and what does not?

tools.title: Formation / Practical-Wisdom Audit
tools.function: Examine how habits and practices form practical perception and judgment.
tools.question: What is this practice forming people to notice, enjoy, avoid, choose, and become?

tools.title: Control / Desire / Moral-Range Audit
tools.function: Calibrate agency and responsibility under constraint.
tools.question: What is controllable, influenceable, or outside control?

tools.title: Moral Authority / Common-Good Audit
tools.function: Test whether a rule has moral standing beyond enforceability.
tools.question: Why should this rule bind?

tools.title: Legitimacy / Standing Audit
tools.function: Test who may exercise consequential authority and under what limits.
tools.question: Why may this actor exercise consequential authority here?

tools.title: Perspective / Moral-Visibility Audit
tools.function: Test how other persons are represented and where perspective remains incomplete.
tools.question: Whose situation is being represented, by whom, and with what limits?

tools.title: Respect / Duty / Autonomy Audit
tools.function: Test whether an action preserves another person as an agent.
tools.question: Does this action preserve the person as an agent rather than merely manage them?

tools.title: Consequence / Welfare / Harm Audit
tools.function: Evaluate effects, uncertainty, distribution, and coercion.
tools.question: Who is affected, what happens, how certain are we, and who bears the burden?

tools.title: Background Power / Genealogy Audit
tools.function: Inspect conditions shaping choices, categories, and values before explicit decisions occur.
tools.question: What is shaping the choice before the choice appears?

tools.title: Fair-Structure / Veil-of-Ignorance Audit
tools.function: Evaluate institutional rules without privileging one's present position.
tools.question: Would I choose these rules without knowing which position would be mine?

tools.title: Dependency / Effective-Capability Audit
tools.function: Test whether nominal resources become real possibilities for action.
tools.question: What can this person actually do and be under these conditions?

failures.title: Map Substitution
failures.symptom: A representation is treated as though it were the thing represented.
failures.diagnosticQuestion: What did I actually observe, and what did the map add?

failures.title: Omission Failure
failures.symptom: Relevant actors, facts, burdens, perspectives, or uncertainty never enter the map.
failures.diagnosticQuestion: What important thing or person is missing?

failures.title: Inferential Overreach
failures.symptom: The conclusion says more than the reasons establish.
failures.diagnosticQuestion: What is the strongest conclusion these reasons actually support?

failures.title: Direction-of-Justification Failure
failures.symptom: Something requiring justification is used as its own justification.
failures.diagnosticQuestion: What is supposed to explain what?

failures.title: Formation Blindness
failures.symptom: Choice is analyzed without examining practices that formed perception and judgment.
failures.diagnosticQuestion: What has this practice trained agents to notice or ignore?

failures.title: Agency Miscalibration
failures.symptom: Responsibility is assigned without regard to control or constraint.
failures.diagnosticQuestion: What was actually within the agent's range?

failures.title: Authority Substitution
failures.symptom: Power, office, expertise, or enforcement is mistaken for moral standing.
failures.diagnosticQuestion: Why may this actor decide or impose this?

failures.title: Agency Bypass
failures.symptom: A beneficial intervention treats a person as an object to manage rather than an agent.
failures.diagnosticQuestion: Was the person preserved as an agent?

failures.title: Aggregation Blindness
failures.symptom: Total or average benefit hides who bears burdens.
failures.diagnosticQuestion: Who gains, who loses, and how are burdens distributed?

failures.title: Causal Confidence Inflation
failures.symptom: Prediction, correlation, or association is treated as stronger causal knowledge than the evidence supports.
failures.diagnosticQuestion: What causal claim has actually been earned?

failures.title: Background-Condition Blindness
failures.symptom: A choice is treated as self-contained although structures shaped its available options.
failures.diagnosticQuestion: What shaped the choice field before the choice appeared?

failures.title: Genealogical Fallacy
failures.symptom: Showing how a belief or value arose is treated as proving it false.
failures.diagnosticQuestion: Does this origin story actually bear on validity?

failures.title: Procedural Neutrality Illusion
failures.symptom: A formally identical rule is assumed fair despite unequal background positions.
failures.diagnosticQuestion: Would the rule remain acceptable without knowing my position?

failures.title: Resource/Capability Collapse
failures.symptom: Having a resource or formal opportunity is treated as equivalent to being able to use it.
failures.diagnosticQuestion: What can the person actually do with the nominal resource?

failures.title: Judgment/Authorization Collapse
failures.symptom: Evidence sufficient for belief is treated as sufficient for intervention.
failures.diagnosticQuestion: What action is actually authorized by this evidence and standing?

failures.title: Closure Inflation
failures.symptom: A present judgment is treated as permanently settled.
failures.diagnosticQuestion: What would require us to reopen this judgment?

claimCeilings.text: Evidence does not license a stronger conclusion than it supports.

cases.title: Foucault and the Measurement of Light Speed
cases.question: How much can a discriminating experiment actually establish?
cases.summary: Instrumental capability can make previously inaccessible differences publicly discriminable without settling every ontological question.

states.label: Pre-discrimination
states.text: Competing optical accounts imply different expectations while terrestrial discrimination remains difficult.

states.label: Instrumental discrimination
states.text: Rotating optical apparatus makes a previously inaccessible timing relation measurable.

states.label: Bounded reconstruction
states.text: The result changes comparative standing while stronger ontological claims remain separately licensed.

transitions.label: New instrument opens a discriminating observation.
Result is retained while its claim ceiling is made explicit.

probes.title: Auxiliary reopening probe
probes.prompt: Which auxiliary commitments could be revised while preserving the measured relation?

cases.reopen: REOPEN if stronger source work changes what the experiment was taken to discriminate.

cases.title: Neptune / Vulcan
cases.question: Why can the same repair strategy succeed once and fail later?
cases.summary: A successful unseen-body repair in the Neptune case did not turn auxiliary repair into a universal rule for later anomalies.

states.label: Anomaly
states.text: Observed motion departs from the current model's expectation.

states.label: Neptune auxiliary hypothesis
states.text: An unseen planet is proposed as a perturbing body.

states.label: Neptune confirmation
states.text: Prediction guides observation and the repair gains strong standing.

states.label: Mercury/Vulcan pressure
states.text: A similar unseen-body strategy is applied to Mercury's residual discrepancy.

states.label: Framework revision
states.text: Vulcan lacks stable confirmation; general relativity later reorganizes the gravitational framework.

transitions.label: Prediction and observation support the repair.
Failed auxiliary repair is followed by deeper framework revision.

probes.title: Neptune repair-world probe
probes.prompt: What additional observations should follow if the unseen-body repair is right?

probes.title: Vulcan comparator probe
probes.prompt: What changes if the auxiliary is retained versus the gravitational framework revised?
probes.firewall: Successful strategy in one case ≠ universal revision rule.

cases.reopen: REOPEN when new evidence changes the comparative standing of auxiliary and framework revisions.

cases.title: Galileo and Telescopic Astronomy
cases.question: How do new instruments alter what can count as publicly inspectable evidence?
cases.summary: Telescopic observations altered the evidence field and pressured inherited celestial categories without each observation deductively proving the entire Copernican system.

states.label: Inherited celestial map
states.text: Pre-telescopic categories organize the terrestrial/celestial distinction.

states.label: Telescopic evidence
states.text: Lunar topography, Jovian satellites, phases of Venus, and related observations alter the publicly inspectable evidence field.

states.label: Interpretive and institutional dispute
states.text: Evidence, interpretation, demonstration, standing, and authority become coupled but non-identical issues.

transitions.label: New evidence pressures inherited categories and shifts the dispute.

probes.title: Instrumental evidence probe
probes.prompt: Which inherited claims are directly pressured by the observations, and which require further inference?

probes.title: Standing probe
probes.prompt: What changes if institutional authority is altered while observational evidence is held fixed?

cases.reopen: REOPEN if source work changes the historical reconstruction of what observations licensed.

cases.title: Newton → Einstein
cases.question: How can a later framework transform concepts while preserving bounded earlier successes?
cases.summary: General relativity reorganizes gravitation while Newtonian mechanics retains strong practical standing in bounded regimes.

states.label: Newtonian framework
states.text: A highly successful gravitational framework supports broad prediction and explanation.

states.label: Relativistic reconstruction
states.text: Space, time, gravity, and admissible description are reorganized within relativity.

states.label: Domain-bounded continuity
states.text: Newtonian results remain powerful approximations in appropriate regimes.

transitions.label: Framework and conceptual relations are revised.
Predecessor success is retained under explicit domain limits.

probes.title: Equivalence probe
probes.prompt: What can be made locally equivalent, and what remainder appears when scale or tidal structure is restored?

cases.reopen: REOPEN if the comparison task or scale changes.

cases.title: DESI 2024 → 2026
cases.role: Live frontier inquiry and claim-ceiling revision
cases.question: What should accumulating but model-dependent tension do to the standing of the baseline cosmological model?
cases.summary: DESI is represented as a diachronic evidence record: increasing precision can strengthen, weaken, or reorganize model preference without automatically settling ontology.

states.label: 2024 first-year frontier
states.text: First-year BAO results open a serious model-comparison question without licensing discovery language.

states.label: 2025 DR2 three-year update
states.text: A larger dataset strengthens some combined-data hints of evolving dark energy.

states.label: 2026 extended evidence state
states.text: The planned survey observations are completed and later DR2 Lyman-alpha full-shape results add tighter constraints; the newest Lyman-alpha result shifts toward ΛCDM relative to earlier evolving-dark-energy preference.

transitions.label: More data tighten constraints and alter model preference.
New probe structure and full-shape information reorganize the evidence frontier.

probes.title: Dataset-combination probe
probes.prompt: How does model preference change across allowed combinations of DESI and other cosmological data?

probes.title: BAO versus full-shape probe
probes.prompt: What changes when the full Lyman-alpha correlation shape is used rather than BAO-only information?
probes.firewall: Greater precision ≠ guaranteed persistence of an earlier hint.

cases.reopen: REOPEN with new DESI releases, independent probes, or materially changed model comparison.

projections.title: Ethical History
projections.rule: Historical narrative and workbook projection; canonical Tool identity remains in CT-Txx.

projections.title: History of Inquiry
projections.rule: Projects evidence, instrumentation, model, concept, standing, and diachronic transition.

projections.title: Philosophy of Science
projections.rule: Owns narrative treatment while shared formal concepts remain encyclopedia-owned.
